The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) is the oldest and most well-known U.S. stock index, while the S&P 500 represents a broader view of the market with 500 large-cap American stocks. While they are key indicators of U.S. market trends, the two indices differ in structure: the DJIA is price-weighted, meaning higher-priced stocks have more influence, while the S&P 500 is market cap-weighted, reflecting the size of companies. ## US stock futures ticked higher on Tuesday after the major indexes kicked off the week with solid gains, supported by falling oil prices and a strong rally in heavyweight technology stocks. During Monday's regular session, the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite surged 2.13%, while the S&P 500 and Dow advanced 1.48% and 1.32%, respectively.
